title: Tenant-aware quality containment and cross-environment remediation playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Provide a single, tenant-aware playbook for containing model-rollout quality regressions across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. This ticket captures the operational choreography, automated mitigations, tenant communication templates, engineering fixes, and post-incident follow-ups so that when a canary or early rollout shows regression signals we can quickly isolate affected tenants, minimize blast radius, and restore safe behavior with minimal user disruption.

Scope:
- Detection signals and thresholds (quality regressions, hallucination spike, safety classifier failures, throughput anomalies during canary).
- Containment actions per deployment type: Hosted (fast routing/pinning), Dedicated (capacity-aware pin + evacuation), Private (customer liaison + in-place patch guidance).
- Automated mitigations: model pinning, traffic re-routing, KV cache reconciliation, forced cache invalidation scripts, progressive time-based throttles.
- Communication: internal escalation ladder, customer-facing templates, and status updates cadence.
- Engineering fixes: hotpatch guidance, coordinated PR checklist, and smoke/regression tests to verify rollback correctness.
- Postmortem artifacts: incident timeline, root cause signposts, follow-up projects to reduce recurrence.

Runbook highlights (concise):
1) Triage & classification (first 10 minutes):
   - Verify metric deltas: generation quality score, safety filter hits, conversational context error rate, and customer-reported examples. Compare canary slice vs baseline.
   - Determine environment and tenant slice affected (hosted global, dedicated pool ID, or private tenant).
   - If >= 2 tenants impacted or major commercial customer reports, set priority P0 and trigger Incident Bridge.

2) Immediate containment (10–30 minutes):
   - Hosted: push automated pin to previous model variant for affected tenant IDs via routing config (runtime pinning API). Enable temporary increased sampling to confirm improvement.
   - Dedicated: pin pool routing on the control plane and reduce concurrent requests to pool to drain in-flight tokens. If KV cache divergence suspected, run kvcache-reconcile job with tenant-scoped checkpoint.
   - Private: open secure channel to customer (designated SE) and provide exact rollback binary + manifest; if customer permits, initiate remote apply script. If not permitted, provide patch instructions and support window.

3) Short-term mitigation scripts (10–45 minutes):
   - run /scripts/force-kv-invalidate --tenant <tenant-id>
   - run /ops/rollback-pin --target <model-hash> --reason "quality-regression"
   - If rollback not possible, route affected tenant to a lower-latency smaller model variant with safety guardrails.

4) Communication templates:
   - Internal bridge message template with impact summary, timeline, and immediate actions.
   - Customer note: acknowledgement, mitigation applied, ETA for permanent fix, and contact for escalations. Store template in Confluence incident-templates/quality-containment.

5) Release & PR checklist for hotfixes:
   - Add a targeted unit/regression test that reproduces failing prompt if available.
   - Code reviewer from runtime team + one from infra (KV/cache).
   - Deploy to a narrow canary slice first (0.1%), run smoke suite, then promote.
   - Include automated rollback policy attached to rollout.

6) Metrics to validate success:
   - Customer-reported examples resolved (0 or acceptable threshold).
   - Quality score delta regained to within 95% of baseline.
   - No increase in latency beyond SLOs for pinned model path.

Deployment-specific notes: Hosted: we can enact pins and routing changes immediately; prioritize preserving availability over absolute parity in outputs. Dedicated: coordinate with capacity team to avoid overdraining pools; if pinning reduces throughput, notify Billing/Capacity owners. Private: treat customer as control plane partner — require signed consent for remote apply; maintain audit trail and offer rollback scripts.

Acceptance criteria for when to close this ticket:
- Documented playbook with templated scripts and Confluence runbook link.
- Automated rollback and pin APIs validated in staging with end-to-end tests.
- Communication templates reviewed and approved by Support and Legal.
- At least one tabletop drill completed with oncall and SE teams (evidence linked).

Risks and trade-offs:
- Aggressive global pinning reduces blast radius but may change user-visible outputs for unaffected tenants; prefer tenant-scoped pins where possible.
- For Dedicated pools, forcing drain may create transient capacity shortages; balance with burst policies.
- Private tenants may refuse remote patches, slowing mitigation; maintain rapid SE support and pre-authorized rollback agreements where possible.

Next steps:
- Finish scripts and add to ops repo (ENG tasks below).
- Schedule tabletop and add to oncall rotation runbooks.
- Coordinate with Support to add template flows and with Legal for private deployment patch consent language.

postmortem_notes: Primary root cause: model variant introduced during staged rollout had a subtle tokenization edge case causing safety classifier to misfire for a small set of prompts. Contributing factor: insufficient regression coverage for long-prefix contexts in the pre-rollout test suite. Action items: add long-prefix regression tests, tighten canary slice config to include representative tenant prompts, and add automated safety-signal alerts to the alerting dashboard.
owner_notes: Keep tenant-scope pins as the default containment strategy. For enterprise/private customers, pre-authorize a ‘remote-apply’ play during onboarding to shorten mitigation time. Ensure all mitigation actions are logged to audit trail with ticket IDs.
